question_or_symptom: A multi-gigabyte logical allocation limit would make an eager in-process backing store consume unbounded host memory and obscure atomic transfer failure.
observation: Most new allocation bytes are zero and a bounded transfer touches only a small set of 64 KiB chunks. Updating chunks while reading a carrier would leave partial state if CRC, allocation, or range validation failed later.
conclusion: Logical allocation accounting and resident sparse backing accounting require distinct limits and commit points.
decision: Represent absent chunks as implicit zero, enforce independent live-allocation, logical-byte, transfer-byte, and resident-chunk bounds, prepare every H2D chunk and verify the full carrier CRC before atomically publishing any changed bytes, and reclaim all owned chunks on free or disconnect.
invalidated_assumptions: A logical allocation must eagerly reserve an equal amount of host memory.
Per-chunk writes are acceptably atomic for a multi-chunk transfer.
